issues.description: Template file `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` declares `public class AnimalFarm` instead of the required `Farm` class. The problem statement/UML and the reference solution consistently use `Farm`, and `Main.java`'s example code also instantiates `new Farm()`. This naming mismatch breaks the mapping to the specification and will cause compilation errors if students follow the instructions or uncomment `Main`.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template, rename `public class AnimalFarm` to `public class Farm` (keeping the file name `Farm.java`) so it matches the UML/problem statement and the intended usage in `Main`.

issues.description: Template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` is syntactically invalid: inside method `singFarmSong()` it contains a second `package de.tum.cit.ase;` declaration and a duplicated nested `public class AnimalFarm { ... }` block. This prevents the starter code from compiling at all, blocking students from starting the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template `Farm.java` with a single, valid top-level class (named `Farm`) and remove the embedded `package` statement and duplicated class definition from inside `singFarmSong()`.
